concepts.def: A detailed written account of a culture produced by an anthropologist after extended first-hand fieldwork living among the people being studied.
A core fieldwork method in which the anthropologist takes part in the daily life of a community while simultaneously observing and recording its practices.
The extended period, often a year or more, an anthropologist spends living within a community to gather data through immersion and direct experience.
An account of a culture expressed in terms of the insiders' own concepts, categories and meanings as understood by members of that society.
An account of a culture framed using the analytical concepts and comparative categories of the outside observer or anthropologist.
The practice whereby anthropologists critically examine how their own background, presence and assumptions shape the data they collect and how they interpret it.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Anthropological Practice — a core area of Social and Cultural Anthropology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Anthropological Practice brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Anthropological Practice.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The central data-gathering method of social and cultural anthropology is:
options: Participant observation
The laboratory experiment
The postal questionnaire
Random sampling

mcqs.q: An 'emic' account describes a culture using:
options: The insiders' own concepts and meanings
The observer's scientific categories
Statistical averages
Universal natural laws

mcqs.q: When an anthropologist reflects on how their own presence affects the community studied, they are practising:
options: Reflexivity
Generalisation
Quantification
Replication
Living among a community for a prolonged period
Conducting a single brief interview
Analysing existing statistics only
Running controlled clinical trials

mcqs.q: What does 'participant observation' require the anthropologist to do?
options: Simply watch from a distance without any involvement.
Emic refers to economics and etic to ethics.
Hand out questionnaires and then leave immediately.
Take part in the community's daily life while observing and recording it.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an emic and an etic account?
options: Hand out questionnaires and then leave immediately.
Emic refers to economics and etic to ethics.
An emic account uses the insiders' own concepts; an etic account uses the observer's analytical categories.
They mean exactly the same thing.
Because it speeds up data collection.
Emic refers to economics and etic to ethics.
Because it makes research completely objective and bias-free.
Because the researcher's own background and presence shape the data and its interpretation.
